title: The Crocodile
description:
The crocodile is always there. Sometimes you see him, sometimes he sinks beneath the surface, but be assured he is watching. —
The Crocodile is many things.
You have your own Crocodile; just over there, lying in wait.
Even if you can’t admit it to yourself, even if you close your eyes.

Meditating on and agonising over the persistence of chronic illness, generational curses, the rigidity of femininity, and substance abuse, Motormouth Comics presents a collection of terrible beasts and beloved airheads.

title: Miscreants
description:
/ˈmɪskriənt/ (noun): a person who has done something wrong or unlawful. A person behaving badly.

We are eels on the grass in the hot hot sun, slithering desperately for the lake, finding only dwindling pools. Our bodies tire, our once-soft skin blisters and bursts as gills choke on air. Do not despair; this is from no moral failing. You cannot find the lake because it was taken from you. Bit by bit it was drained, poisoned, filled in for a carpark, petrol station, new subdivision. The next puddle isn’t far now, let’s go there together. If we make it I’ll buy you a drink.

title: UNHENGED!
description: A group show investigating the many different kinds of henges in our world.

title: Phantasmagoria
description:
Kudos Offsite Presents:
‘Phantasmagoria’, a two person show featuring Lily Langley and Yvette Nemeth.
Welcome to Phantasmagoria, the birth of a new world.

Artists Yvette Nemeth and Lily Langley AKA Motormouth Comics present mythology melded with modern narratives to fabricate new myths of healing, trauma, and lived experience.

title: Hoons & Goons
description:
“The Worst Bunch of Girls You Ever Met”

The characters present within the Hoons & Goons series are the social circle that is formed through the shared experience of evenings in the pub or parking at the 7/11 to show off your car. There is an inescapable love and hate that is created when you can’t stop running into someone you know. These lot are the last standing goons left behind on a Thursday night when everyone else has gone home for the night, kicked out of one pub and on their way to another with longer opening hours. Whether or not they’ll be let in has not begun to cross their minds, but it’s crossing ours.

title: Death in Suburbia
description: ‘Death in Suburbia’ is a series of collagraphs depicting death as a mundane eventuality as opposed to an ongoing threat. Death comes to us all, but until then he is our neighbour; just someone who lives down the road, who might be sometimes observed taking out his bins or mowing the lawn. The series takes us through a day in the domestic absurd life of death.
